html:
Golconda is a fortress city on the edge of Hyderabad, capital of the Qutb Shahi sultans from 1518 to 1687. On the 1783 map its name still marks the lands of the Nizam of Hyderabad.

The Qutb Shahi dynasty broke away from the Bahmani Sultanate and ruled the Telugu country. The old fort had first been built in mud by the Kakatiyas. In 1591 Sultan Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah founded Hyderabad nearby, with the Charminar at its centre.

Golconda was famous for diamonds from the Krishna valley mines, among them perhaps the Koh-i-Noor, and for steel; see wootz steel. Its ports traded cloth across the Bay of Bengal. In 1687 Aurangzeb took the fort after an eight month siege, and Golconda became a Mughal province. In 1724 its governor, the Nizam, made himself independent.
